record.paper_title: An open problem: Why are motif-avoidant attractors so rare in asynchronous Boolean networks?
record.original_question: How does node deletion reduction or model compression change motif avoidance in Boolean networks, and which conditions determine whether deleting non-self-regulating variables creates a new motif-avoidant attractor, destroys an existing motif-avoidant attractor by creating a stable motif or minimal trap space, or changes the network without producing motif avoidance? The question should cover both biological Boolean model reductions and random Boolean network reductions, because reduction can increase density and alter reachability in non-local ways.

evidence.quote: As we have seen, node deletion can, in practice, lead to the introduction of MAAs.
The emergence of these motif-avoidant attractors motivates further study into the relationship between node deletion and motif avoidance.

Our analysis demonstrates that even though motif-avoidant attractors are extremely rare in both biological and random networks, network reduction does meaningfully alter the likelihood of their presence.
Our results caution against the indiscriminate use of compression during modeling.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let an asynchronous Boolean network be a pair (V,F) where V={x_1,...,x_n} are Boolean variables and F=(f_1,...,f_n) is a collection of update functions f_i:{0,1}^n→{0,1}. Its asynchronous state-transition graph has vertex set {0,1}^n; from a state s there is an edge to every state obtained by flipping a single coordinate x_i with s_i ≠ f_i(s). An attractor is a terminal strongly connected component of this graph. A trap space is a subcube of {0,1}^n that is forward-invariant under the asynchronous dynamics; a minimal trap space is one that contains no proper trap subspace. An attractor is called motif-avoidant (an MAA) if it is not contained in any minimal trap space.

A variable x_i is non-self-regulating if f_i does not depend on x_i. Node-deletion reduction with respect to such a variable produces a Boolean network on V∖{x_i} by substituting f_i into the remaining update functions wherever x_i appears.

Problem. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on (V,F) and on a non-self-regulating variable x_i under which the node-deletion reduction:
(a) creates a motif-avoidant attractor in the reduced network that has no counterpart in the original network;
(b) destroys an existing motif-avoidant attractor by causing it to be absorbed into a newly created stable motif or minimal trap space of the reduced network;
(c) modifies the network without affecting the presence or absence of motif-avoidant attractors.

Provide a characterization that applies both to Boolean models of biological regulatory systems and to random Boolean networks, and that accounts for the fact that reduction can increase the density of regulatory interactions and alter reachability in the state-transition graph in non-local ways.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem motivating further study of the relationship between node deletion and motif avoidance in asynchronous Boolean networks. Empirical observations show node-deletion reduction can both create and destroy motif-avoidant attractors, but no general characterizing conditions appear to be known. Related work on asynchronous Boolean network reduction (e.g., elimination of negatively autoregulated components) establishes attractor-preservation results in restricted settings, but does not resolve the general question.

status_evidence.title: An open problem: Why are motif-avoidant attractors so rare in asynchronous Boolean networks?
status_evidence.snippet: Using node deletion reduction, researchers found several MAAs in reduced versions of biological Boolean models; node reduction can also eliminate an MAA by transforming it into a regular complex attractor.
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between node-deletion reduction and motif avoidance is identified as an open problem motivating further study.

status_evidence.title: Reduction for asynchronous Boolean networks: elimination of negatively autoregulated components
status_evidence.snippet: Reduction methods for asynchronous Boolean networks with attractor-preservation guarantees in restricted cases.
status_evidence.claim: Existing reduction results are restricted and do not yield a general characterization of when reduction creates or destroys MAAs.
